questions.question: What is the difference between JDK, JRE, and JVM?
questions.answer: JVM (Java Virtual Machine) executes Java bytecode. JRE (Java Runtime Environment) includes JVM and libraries. JDK (Java Development Kit) includes JRE plus development tools like compiler.

questions.question: What are the four pillars of OOP?
questions.answer: Encapsulation, Inheritance, Polymorphism, and Abstraction. They are fundamental concepts for designing object-oriented systems.

questions.question: What is the difference between == and .equals()?
questions.answer: == compares object references (memory addresses), while .equals() compares object values. For strings, .equals() is preferred.

questions.question: What is the difference between ArrayList and LinkedList?
questions.answer: ArrayList uses dynamic arrays (fast random access), LinkedList uses doubly-linked lists (fast insertion/deletion). ArrayList is better for access, LinkedList for modifications.

questions.question: What is the difference between synchronized and volatile?
questions.answer: synchronized provides mutual exclusion and memory visibility, volatile only ensures visibility of changes. synchronized is for thread safety, volatile for visibility.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'final' keyword?
questions.answer: final prevents modification. For classes: prevents inheritance. For methods: prevents overriding. For variables: makes them immutable.

questions.question: What is the difference between checked and unchecked exceptions?
questions.answer: Checked exceptions must be caught or declared (IOException, SQLException). Unchecked exceptions don't require handling (NullPointerException, RuntimeException).

questions.question: What is the difference between abstract class and interface?
questions.answer: Abstract classes can have state and constructors, interfaces cannot. Classes extend one abstract class but implement multiple interfaces. Interfaces define contracts, abstract classes provide partial implementation.

questions.question: What are generics in Java?
questions.answer: Generics enable type-safe collections and methods. They allow you to specify the type of objects a collection can hold, detected at compile-time.

questions.question: What is the difference between HashMap and Hashtable?
questions.answer: HashMap is unsynchronized and allows null keys/values, Hashtable is synchronized and doesn't allow nulls. HashMap is preferred in modern Java.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'static' keyword?
questions.answer: static creates class-level members shared by all instances. Static variables are initialized once, static methods can be called without object instantiation.

questions.question: What is a deadlock and how to prevent it?
questions.answer: Deadlock occurs when threads wait for each other indefinitely. Prevent by: acquiring locks in order, using timeouts, avoiding nested locks, or using concurrent utilities.

questions.question: What is garbage collection in Java?
questions.answer: Garbage collection automatically frees memory by removing unreferenced objects. JVM manages this, reducing manual memory management burden.

questions.question: What are Java Streams and their advantages?
questions.answer: Streams provide functional-style operations on collections. They support lazy evaluation, parallel processing, and enable declarative data transformations.

questions.question: What is method overloading?
questions.answer: Method overloading allows multiple methods with the same name but different parameters. Resolved at compile-time based on parameter types/count.

questions.question: What is method overriding?
questions.answer: Method overriding allows a subclass to provide a specific implementation of a parent class method. Resolved at runtime using polymorphism.

questions.question: What is the difference between String, StringBuilder, and StringBuffer?
questions.answer: String is immutable, StringBuilder is mutable and not synchronized, StringBuffer is mutable and synchronized. Use StringBuilder for performance in single-threaded code.

questions.question: What is the difference between Set, List, and Map?
questions.answer: List maintains order and allows duplicates, Set doesn't allow duplicates, Map stores key-value pairs. Each has different use cases.

questions.question: What are annotations in Java?
questions.answer: Annotations provide metadata about code without affecting code execution. Examples: @Override, @Deprecated, @SuppressWarnings. Used by compiler and runtime.

questions.question: What is the 'this' keyword in Java?
questions.answer: 'this' refers to the current object instance. Used to access instance variables, call constructors, or pass the current object as parameter.

questions.question: What is the 'super' keyword in Java?
questions.answer: 'super' refers to the parent class. Used to call parent constructors, access parent methods, or access parent variables.

questions.question: What is try-with-resources?
questions.answer: try-with-resources automatically closes resources implementing AutoCloseable. Simplifies resource management and prevents resource leaks.

questions.question: What is the difference between wait() and sleep()?
questions.answer: wait() releases the lock and waits for notification, sleep() holds the lock and pauses execution. wait() is for synchronization, sleep() for delays.

questions.question: What is the difference between pass-by-value and pass-by-reference?
questions.answer: Java is pass-by-value. For primitives, values are copied. For objects, references are copied, so modifications affect the original object.

questions.question: What is reflection in Java?
questions.answer: Reflection allows inspecting and modifying classes, methods, and fields at runtime. Enables dynamic loading, instantiation, and method invocation.

questions.question: What is type erasure in generics?
questions.answer: Type erasure removes generic type information at compile-time for backward compatibility. Generic types become Object at runtime.

questions.question: What is composition and aggregation?
questions.answer: Composition is a strong 'has-a' relationship where child cannot exist without parent. Aggregation is a weak 'has-a' relationship where child can exist independently.

questions.question: What is the default value of instance variables?
questions.answer: Numeric types default to 0, boolean to false, objects to null. Local variables have no default and must be initialized.

questions.question: What is the difference between Iterator and ListIterator?
questions.answer: Iterator moves forward only, ListIterator moves both directions. ListIterator can add/remove elements, Iterator only removes.

questions.question: What are intermediate and terminal operations in Streams?
questions.answer: Intermediate operations (map, filter) return Stream for chaining. Terminal operations (collect, forEach) return non-Stream results and trigger execution.

questions.question: What is a thread pool and ExecutorService?
questions.answer: Thread pool manages reusable threads. ExecutorService provides methods to submit tasks and manage thread lifecycle efficiently.

questions.question: What is the difference between class and object?
questions.answer: Class is a blueprint/template, object is an instance of a class. Class is logical, object is physical with actual values.

questions.question: What is encapsulation?
questions.answer: Encapsulation hides internal implementation details using access modifiers (private, protected, public). Provides data protection and controlled access.

questions.question: What is the difference between constructor and method?
questions.answer: Constructor initializes objects and has the same name as class, method performs actions. Constructors are called once during object creation, methods multiple times.

questions.question: What is constructor overloading?
questions.answer: Constructor overloading allows multiple constructors with different parameters in the same class. Provides flexibility in object initialization.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'new' keyword?
questions.answer: 'new' allocates memory for a new object and calls the constructor. It creates an instance of a class on the heap.

questions.question: What is the difference between TreeMap and HashMap?
questions.answer: HashMap uses hash table (unordered), TreeMap uses red-black tree (sorted). TreeMap maintains order, HashMap is faster for lookup.

questions.question: What is the difference between HashSet and TreeSet?
questions.answer: HashSet uses hash table (unordered), TreeSet uses red-black tree (sorted). TreeSet maintains order, HashSet is faster.

questions.question: What is the difference between map() and flatMap()?
questions.answer: map() transforms each element, flatMap() transforms and flattens nested streams. Use flatMap() when transformation returns a stream.

questions.question: What is the volatile keyword?
questions.answer: volatile ensures visibility of changes across threads. Prevents compiler optimizations that might cache values, guaranteeing fresh reads from memory.

questions.question: What is polymorphism?
questions.answer: Polymorphism allows objects to take multiple forms. Enables method overloading (compile-time) and overriding (runtime), providing flexibility and extensibility.

questions.question: What is the difference between primitive and reference types?
questions.answer: Primitive types (int, boolean) store values directly, reference types (objects) store memory addresses. Primitives are stack-allocated, references are heap-allocated.

questions.question: What is the difference between Queue and Deque?
questions.answer: Queue is FIFO (First-In-First-Out), Deque is double-ended allowing insertion/removal from both ends. Deque is more flexible than Queue.

questions.question: What is the difference between throw and throws?
questions.answer: throw explicitly throws an exception, throws declares that a method may throw exceptions. throw is used in method body, throws in method signature.

questions.question: What is the difference between break and continue?
questions.answer: break exits the loop entirely, continue skips the current iteration and proceeds to the next. Both are used in loops and switch statements.

questions.question: What is inheritance?
questions.answer: Inheritance allows a class to inherit properties and methods from another class. Promotes code reuse and establishes 'is-a' relationships.

questions.question: What is the difference between public, private, and protected?
questions.answer: public is accessible everywhere, private only within the class, protected within package and subclasses. Control visibility and encapsulation.

questions.question: What is a race condition?
questions.answer: Race condition occurs when multiple threads access shared data concurrently without synchronization, leading to unpredictable results. Prevent with synchronization.

questions.question: What is the difference between Comparable and Comparator?
questions.answer: Comparable is implemented by the class itself (compareTo), Comparator is external comparison logic. Comparable is natural ordering, Comparator is custom ordering.

questions.question: What is the difference between instance and static variables?
questions.answer: Instance variables are created per object, static variables are shared across all instances. Instance variables have separate values, static variables have one value.

questions.question: What are wildcards in generics?
questions.answer: Wildcards (?) provide flexibility in generic types. ? extends Type (upper bound), ? super Type (lower bound), ? (unbounded). Enable covariance and contravariance.

questions.question: What is the difference between peek() and forEach()?
questions.answer: peek() is intermediate operation for debugging, forEach() is terminal operation. peek() returns Stream, forEach() returns void.

questions.question: What is the difference between heap and stack?
questions.answer: Stack stores primitives and references (LIFO), heap stores objects. Stack is faster but limited, heap is larger but slower. Stack is thread-safe, heap requires synchronization.

questions.question: What is an abstract class?
questions.answer: Abstract class cannot be instantiated, provides partial implementation. Contains abstract methods (no body) and concrete methods. Used as base for related classes.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'instanceof' operator?
questions.answer: 'instanceof' checks if an object is an instance of a class or interface. Returns boolean, used for type checking before casting.

questions.question: What is the difference between fail-fast and fail-safe iterators?
questions.answer: Fail-fast throws ConcurrentModificationException if collection is modified during iteration. Fail-safe works on a copy, allowing modifications.

questions.question: What is the difference between Runnable and Callable?
questions.answer: Runnable returns void, Callable returns a value. Runnable cannot throw checked exceptions, Callable can. Callable is used with ExecutorService.

questions.question: What is the difference between array and ArrayList?
questions.answer: Array has fixed size, ArrayList is dynamic. Array can store primitives, ArrayList stores objects. Array is faster, ArrayList is more flexible.

questions.question: What is an interface?
questions.answer: Interface defines a contract with abstract methods. Classes implement interfaces to provide concrete implementations. Enables multiple inheritance of type.

questions.question: What is the difference between collect() and reduce()?
questions.answer: collect() accumulates elements into a container, reduce() combines elements into a single value. collect() returns container, reduce() returns single value.

questions.question: What is a Future and CompletableFuture?
questions.answer: Future represents a result available in the future. CompletableFuture allows manual completion and chaining of async operations. CompletableFuture is more powerful.

questions.question: What is the difference between length and length()?
questions.answer: length is a property of arrays, length() is a method of strings. Both return the number of elements/characters.

questions.question: What is the difference between ConcurrentHashMap and synchronized HashMap?
questions.answer: ConcurrentHashMap uses bucket-level locking (better concurrency), synchronized HashMap locks the entire map. ConcurrentHashMap is preferred for multi-threaded access.

questions.question: What is the difference between IS-A and HAS-A relationships?
questions.answer: IS-A is inheritance (class extends another), HAS-A is composition (class contains another). IS-A represents specialization, HAS-A represents aggregation.

questions.question: What is the difference between == and .equals() for strings?
questions.answer: == compares string references, .equals() compares string values. Use .equals() for content comparison, == for reference comparison.

questions.question: What is the finally block?
questions.answer: finally block executes regardless of exception occurrence. Used for cleanup (closing resources). Executes even if return/throw is in try/catch.

questions.question: What is a semaphore?
questions.answer: Semaphore controls access to a resource using a counter. Acquire decrements counter, release increments. Used to limit concurrent access to resources.

questions.question: What is the difference between while and do-while loops?
questions.answer: while checks condition before execution, do-while checks after. do-while executes at least once, while may not execute at all.

questions.question: What is the difference between PriorityQueue and Queue?
questions.answer: PriorityQueue orders elements by priority, Queue is FIFO. PriorityQueue uses heap, Queue uses array/linked list. PriorityQueue is useful for priority-based processing.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'package' keyword?
questions.answer: 'package' organizes classes into namespaces. Prevents naming conflicts, controls access, and improves code organization.

questions.question: What is the difference between import and import static?
questions.answer: import imports a class or package, import static imports static members. import static allows using static members without class prefix.

questions.question: What is lazy evaluation in Streams?
questions.answer: Streams don't process elements until a terminal operation is called. Intermediate operations are lazy, improving performance by avoiding unnecessary processing.

questions.question: What is a CountDownLatch?
questions.answer: CountDownLatch allows one or more threads to wait for operations to complete. Threads wait at await(), others call countDown(). Used for synchronization.

questions.question: What is the difference between String concatenation and String.format()?
questions.answer: String concatenation uses + operator, String.format() uses format specifiers. format() is more readable for complex strings, concatenation is simpler.

questions.question: What is the difference between Collections.sort() and Arrays.sort()?
questions.answer: Collections.sort() sorts lists, Arrays.sort() sorts arrays. Collections.sort() uses merge sort, Arrays.sort() uses quicksort/dual-pivot quicksort.

questions.question: What is the difference between class and inner class?
questions.answer: Class is top-level, inner class is nested within another class. Inner class has access to outer class members, can be static or non-static.

questions.question: What is the difference between null and empty string?
questions.answer: null means no value assigned, empty string is a string with no characters. null requires null check, empty string can be checked with .isEmpty().

questions.question: What is the difference between Exception and Error?
questions.answer: Exception is recoverable (checked/unchecked), Error is not recoverable (OutOfMemoryError, StackOverflowError). Catch Exception, not Error.

questions.question: What is a CyclicBarrier?
questions.answer: CyclicBarrier allows multiple threads to wait for each other at a barrier point. Threads call await(), all proceed when count reached. Reusable unlike CountDownLatch.

questions.question: What is the difference between for and enhanced for loop?
questions.answer: for loop uses index, enhanced for loop iterates over elements directly. Enhanced for is simpler for collections, for loop provides index access.

questions.question: What is the difference between sequential and parallel streams?
questions.answer: Sequential streams process elements one by one, parallel streams use multiple threads. Parallel is faster for large datasets, sequential for small or ordered data.

questions.question: What is the difference between WeakHashMap and HashMap?
questions.answer: WeakHashMap uses weak references for keys (garbage collected if no strong references), HashMap uses strong references. WeakHashMap is useful for caches.

questions.question: What is the difference between static and non-static inner class?
questions.answer: Static inner class doesn't have access to outer class instance, non-static does. Static inner class can be instantiated without outer instance, non-static cannot.

questions.question: What is the difference between char and String?
questions.answer: char is a single character (primitive), String is a sequence of characters (object). char uses single quotes, String uses double quotes.

questions.question: What is the difference between notify() and notifyAll()?
questions.answer: notify() wakes one waiting thread, notifyAll() wakes all waiting threads. notifyAll() is safer to avoid missed notifications.

questions.question: What is the difference between int and Integer?
questions.answer: int is primitive type, Integer is wrapper class (object). int is faster, Integer provides utility methods and can be null.

questions.question: What is the difference between CopyOnWriteArrayList and ArrayList?
questions.answer: CopyOnWriteArrayList is thread-safe (copies on write), ArrayList is not. CopyOnWriteArrayList is slower for writes, better for reads.

questions.question: What is the difference between method and function?
questions.answer: Method is a function within a class, function is standalone. In Java, all functions are methods (part of classes).

questions.question: What is the difference between && and &?
questions.answer: && is logical AND (short-circuit), & is bitwise AND. && doesn't evaluate right operand if left is false, & always evaluates both.

questions.question: What is the difference between findFirst() and findAny()?
questions.answer: findFirst() returns first element, findAny() returns any element. findFirst() is deterministic, findAny() is non-deterministic (useful for parallel streams).

questions.question: What is the difference between synchronized method and synchronized block?
questions.answer: Synchronized method locks the entire method, synchronized block locks only a portion. Block is more granular and efficient.

questions.question: What is the difference between || and |?
questions.answer: || is logical OR (short-circuit), | is bitwise OR. || doesn't evaluate right operand if left is true, | always evaluates both.

questions.question: What is the difference between IdentityHashMap and HashMap?
questions.answer: IdentityHashMap uses reference equality (==), HashMap uses value equality (.equals()). IdentityHashMap is faster but less commonly used.

questions.question: What is the difference between clone() and copy constructor?
questions.answer: clone() creates a shallow copy, copy constructor can create deep copy. clone() requires Cloneable interface, copy constructor is more flexible.

questions.question: What is the difference between ! and ~?
questions.answer: ! is logical NOT, ~ is bitwise NOT. ! inverts boolean, ~ inverts all bits in integer.

questions.question: What is the difference between limit() and skip()?
questions.answer: limit() restricts stream to n elements, skip() skips first n elements. Both are intermediate operations for stream slicing.

questions.question: What is the difference between ReentrantLock and synchronized?
questions.answer: ReentrantLock is more flexible (try-lock, fairness), synchronized is simpler. ReentrantLock allows same thread to acquire lock multiple times.

questions.question: What is the difference between % and //?
questions.answer: % is modulo (remainder), // is not a Java operator. Use % for remainder, / for division.

questions.question: What is the difference between EnumMap and HashMap?
questions.answer: EnumMap is optimized for enum keys, HashMap is general-purpose. EnumMap is faster and more memory-efficient for enums.

questions.question: What is the difference between shallow copy and deep copy?
questions.answer: Shallow copy copies references (objects point to same data), deep copy copies actual data. Deep copy is safer but slower.

questions.question: What is the difference between ++ and +=1?
questions.answer: ++ increments by 1, +=1 adds 1. Both are equivalent for integers, ++ has pre and post versions.

questions.question: What is the difference between distinct() and filter()?
questions.answer: distinct() removes duplicates, filter() keeps elements matching predicate. distinct() uses equals(), filter() uses custom logic.

questions.question: What is the difference between Phaser and CyclicBarrier?
questions.answer: Phaser is more flexible (dynamic parties), CyclicBarrier is fixed. Phaser supports multiple phases, CyclicBarrier is single-use per cycle.

questions.question: What is the difference between >> and >>>?
questions.answer: >> is signed right shift (preserves sign), >>> is unsigned right shift (fills with 0). >> for arithmetic, >>> for logical shift.

questions.question: What is the difference between synchronizedList and CopyOnWriteArrayList?
questions.answer: synchronizedList wraps list with synchronized methods, CopyOnWriteArrayList copies on write. CopyOnWriteArrayList is better for read-heavy workloads.

questions.question: What is the difference between interface and abstract class in terms of state?
questions.answer: Abstract class can have state (instance variables), interface cannot (only constants). Abstract class is better for shared state.

questions.question: What is the difference between << and >>?
questions.answer: << is left shift (multiply by 2^n), >> is right shift (divide by 2^n). Both are bitwise operations for efficient arithmetic.

questions.question: What is the difference between sorted() and sort()?
questions.answer: sorted() is stream intermediate operation, sort() is collection method. sorted() returns stream, sort() modifies collection in-place.

questions.question: What is the difference between AtomicInteger and volatile int?
questions.answer: AtomicInteger provides atomic operations, volatile int only ensures visibility. AtomicInteger is safer for concurrent modifications.

questions.question: What is the difference between & and &&?
questions.answer: & is bitwise AND, && is logical AND. & always evaluates both, && short-circuits if left is false.

questions.question: What is the difference between Collections.unmodifiableList() and Arrays.asList()?
questions.answer: unmodifiableList() creates immutable view, Arrays.asList() creates mutable list backed by array. unmodifiableList() prevents modifications.

questions.question: What is the difference between default method and abstract method in interface?
questions.answer: Default method has implementation, abstract method doesn't. Default method is optional to override, abstract method must be implemented.

questions.question: What is the difference between | and ||?
questions.answer: | is bitwise OR, || is logical OR. | always evaluates both, || short-circuits if left is true.

questions.question: What is the difference between anyMatch() and allMatch()?
questions.answer: anyMatch() returns true if any element matches, allMatch() returns true if all match. anyMatch() short-circuits on first match.

questions.question: What is the difference between BlockingQueue and Queue?
questions.answer: BlockingQueue blocks on empty/full, Queue throws exception. BlockingQueue is useful for producer-consumer patterns.

questions.question: What is the difference between ^ and !=?
questions.answer: ^ is bitwise XOR, != is logical not-equal. ^ operates on bits, != operates on boolean values.

questions.question: What is the difference between Collections.emptyList() and new ArrayList()?
questions.answer: emptyList() returns immutable empty list, new ArrayList() returns mutable empty list. emptyList() is more memory-efficient.

questions.question: What is the difference between static final and final?
questions.answer: static final is class constant (shared), final is instance constant (per object). static final is initialized once, final per instance.

questions.question: What is the difference between ternary operator and if-else?
questions.answer: Ternary operator is inline conditional expression, if-else is statement. Ternary is concise for simple conditions, if-else for complex logic.

questions.question: What is the difference between noneMatch() and allMatch()?
questions.answer: noneMatch() returns true if no elements match, allMatch() returns true if all match. noneMatch() is opposite of anyMatch().
